title: fleet-tilt-queue-sync-weekly-catchup-2026-05-27
content:
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Priya, Oliver, Lena (absent: Sam)
Duration: 40m
Objective: weekly sync to capture the new fleet tilt pattern we've been seeing, align on mitigations for next 48h, and decide experiments to run during the capacity window.

1) High-level summary
- Observed a persistent 'tilt' in the scheduling queue since Tue 5/25 where APAC edge nodes build longer queues at 60-90s tail latency while US regions remain in nominal headroom. Tilt appears correlated with a change in the customer routing weight table rolled 5/24 (suspected traffic shift + slightly slower priming).
- Small but consistent increase in cold-kv misses on Apac-edge pods: +18% miss rate vs baseline for 0-4s requests. This amplifies token latency for p99 on medium-length sessions (~256 tokens).
- No GPU hardware alerts; utilization across fleet unchanged (~72% avg). Not a provisioning shortage — the symptom is suboptimal distribution and cache-warmup behavior.

2) Data we reviewed (quick notes)
- Queue depth histogram (5/25-5/27): APAC east queues > 18% of instances have > 8 waiting requests in 99th percentile windows.
- KV cache warmup trace: clients hitting new slot allocation more often (index churn). See link to Linear issue (INF-1213) for trace slices.
- Recent routing change: weight bump to asia-surge-band (rolled 5/24 22:13 UTC). Rolling back locally on canary reduced tilt in that canary by ~45% within 10 minutes.

3) Immediate mitigations (actions for next 48h)
- Rollback candidate: Priya to roll partial rollback of asia-surge-band weight to previous baseline on canary cluster, monitor p99 queue depth and KV miss rate. (Owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-05-27 18:00 UTC)
- Soft-priority smoothing: Ethan to enable a temporary queue-smoothing parameter (alpha=0.6) in allocator for APAC edge for 2 hours during peak to reduce head-of-line build-up. (Owner: Ethan, ETA: 2026-05-27 19:00 UTC)
- Aggressive pre-warm sweep: Run pre-warm job to populate KV caches for the top 12 heavy customers routed to APAC in the last 24h. Script lives in /infra/playbooks/prewarm-apac.sh; Oliver will run and record hit rates. (Owner: Oliver, ETA: 2026-05-28 02:00 UTC)

4) Experiments to run (this week)
- Experiment A: Route-smoothing policy (A/B) — compare current weight table vs smoothed weights with cap on instant changes. Goal: reduce oscillation without increasing cross-region latency. (Owner: Maya + SRE)
- Experiment B: KV aggressive retention for hot prefixes (config: ttl=600->1800s) on a small APAC canary fleet. Measure memory pressure and hit rate delta. (Owner: Priya)
- Experiment C: Priority band multiplexing — allow low-cost batch jobs to be deferred from APAC edge when tilt is detected. (Owner: Ethan)

5) Capacity planning note (next 30 days)
- Headroom target recalibration: propose increasing APAC warm buffer from 8% -> 12% during predicted seasonal peaks (next 3 weekends). This is conservative and will cost ~+3% run cost but expected to reduce emergency spillovers. Need sign-off from capacity finance.
- If tilt persists after routing and cache mitigations, escalate to temporary allocation of two extra multi-tenant GPU slots to APAC (proposal to product: attach with reasoning).

6) Observability gaps we flagged
- Need a higher-resolution KV miss correlation dashboard that ties client-id -> prefix -> request-latency to spot which customers dominate cold start churn. (Owner: Lena)
- Alert tweak: queue-tilt composite alert should include 'recent routing-change' annotation and code pointer to last weight-roll. (Owner: Maya)

7) Notes to self / rough ideas
- Could try a lightweight predictive priming service that watches incoming request hashes and heuristically pre-populates KV for top prefixes (ML-lite model). Prototype in a week? (Maya)
- Consider an auto-fallback policy: if APAC p99 > 3x baseline for >5m, slowly drain new requests to nearest regional fallback instead of immediate full failover. This was discussed previously but never tuned.

8) Blockers / open questions
- How much leeway do we have from finance to temporarily increase APAC buffer in prod? (Finance/Capacity approval required)
- Are there any customer SLAs that prevent cross-region fallback for the set of affected customers? Need CS/legal check.

9) Action items recap
- Priya: partial routing rollback on canary + run TTL canary (due 5/27 18:00 UTC).
- Ethan: enable queue-smoothing alpha and monitor (due 5/27 19:00 UTC).
- Oliver: run pre-warm for top customers and paste hit rate snippets in the ticket (due 5/28 02:00 UTC).
- Lena: draft KV correlation dashboard ticket and initial wireframe (due 5/30).
- Maya: update queue-tilt alert and post this note to Confluence with charts (due 5/28).

10) Follow-up
- Quick standup tomorrow 09:30 PT to check canary metrics and decide if broader rollback is needed.
- Next full infra sync Friday 11:00 PT for retrospective and experiment assignment.

Appendix: quick logs + references
- Linear INF-1213: queue-tilt analysis (traces attached)
- Allocator PR #442: smoothing param addition (link above)
- Prewarm script: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-scripts:prewarm-apac.sh

-- end of notes --

Informal observations: saw a couple odd traces that look like client-side retries from a single SaaS customer (maybe SDK bug). Put on watchlist.
